newsitem.title: CANADA: MPE sees dedicated train runs in flax, malt barley.
newsitem.headline: MPE sees dedicated train runs in flax, malt barley.

text.p: Manitoba Pool Elevators may contract 25-unit trains to exclusively ship flax and malt barley to U.S. crushers and maltsters, MPE's chief executive told reporters at the firm's annual meeting Tuesday.

"That's certainly one of the activities we've identified at Letellier given its location close to the border, access to BN and to some of the big processors in the U.S. in malt barley...and in flax there are processors in the northern United States," MPE's Greg Arason told reporters.
MPE took part in a 100-unit oat train run this fall to Minneapolis where turn around time was cut in half.

"The movement of oats is a good example of what can be done now under the new (deregulated) freight environment. In some cases it may not be 100 cars, it may mean cycling 25 cars which a specific plant can accomodate," Arason said.

MPE is building a 16,000-tonne elevator in Letellier, Man., on a Canadian National Railway Co line about 20 km (12 mi) north of the U.S. border. CN's line connects with a Burlington Northern Santa Fe Corp line.
"There is a lot more flexibility in car allocation now to do the kinds of things that will create efficiency and move product to market at the time that's required," Arason added.
Tenders for the construction of Letellier's elevator should be let shortly with the facility expected to be open in time for the new crop year, he said.
